candidates.name: Outcome Ladder
candidates.quote: The Outcome Ladder separates outcomes into four rungs:
candidates.reason: A core model for defining and measuring different levels of learning success, from recall to real-world transfer.

candidates.name: Friction Budget
candidates.quote: Every learning unit has a friction budget: the maximum mental effort a learner can spend before they quit or start guessing.
candidates.reason: A key concept for designing effective learning by managing cognitive load and learner engagement.

candidates.name: 7-Minute Microlearning Loop
candidates.quote: Use this loop to design one unit: Step 1: Choose one Outcome Ladder rung as the target... Step 7: Add a 'next repetition' prompt...
candidates.reason: A specific, step-by-step method for creating a single microlearning unit from goal-setting to reinforcement.

candidates.name: Spend Friction Where It Buys Transfer
candidates.quote: This does not mean 'make everything easy.' It means you spend friction where it buys transfer.
candidates.reason: A crucial design guideline for allocating learner effort to maximize durable skill application.

candidates.name: Prefer Fewer, Stronger Links
candidates.quote: A note system should connect ideas... But linking every noun creates noise. Links should point to stable concepts, named models, or repeated prerequisites.
candidates.reason: A rule of thumb for effective knowledge structuring, emphasizing quality over quantity in creating connections.

candidates.name: More Content Means More Learning
candidates.quote: Teams often believe that adding more examples and more theory increases learning. In reality, extra content can raise friction without improving transfer.
candidates.reason: Identifies a common error in instructional design that can undermine learning effectiveness.

candidates.name: Recognition Equals Performance
candidates.quote: "If they understood it once, they will perform it later"... Recognition is not performance. People can nod at a good model and still fail under stress.
candidates.reason: Highlights a dangerous misunderstanding about the gap between comprehension and the ability to execute under real conditions.

candidates.name: Two-Speed Feedback
candidates.quote: A guideline for structuring feedback to support both immediate recall and deep understanding, preventing overthinking and blind habit.

candidates.name: Calibration Loop
candidates.quote: A learner calibrates by comparing their choice to an expert choice and understanding the difference. Calibration improves fastest when the learner must commit to a decision before seeing the answer...
candidates.reason: Describes a learning mechanism where judgment is refined through comparison and feedback on underlying variables.

candidates.name: Manager Scenario: Missing Deadlines
candidates.quote: You are a manager. A team member says: 'I keep missing deadlines because other teams block me.'... Action A: Ask for a concrete recent example... Action B: Give advice immediately...
candidates.reason: A concrete, illustrative scenario used to demonstrate the application of a coaching skill and a common error.
